185:             itakura_max_slope=itakura_max_slope,
186:             be=be,
187:         )
188: 
189:         if np.array_equal(current_path, current_path):
190:             break
191: 
192:         current_score = score_match
193: 
194:         if verbose:
195:             print("Iteration {}, score={}".format(it + 1, current_score))
196: 
197:     return current_path, cca, current_score
198: 
199: 
200: def ctw(
201:     s1,
202:     s2,
203:     max_iter=100,
204:     n_components=None,
205:     global_constraint=None,
206:     sakoe_chiba_radius=None,
207:     itakura_max_slope=None,
208:     verbose=False,
209:     be=None,
210: ):
211:     """Compute Canonical Time Warping (CTW) similarity measure between
212:     (possibly multidimensional) time series and return the similarity.
213: 
214:     Canonical Time Warping is a method to align time series under rigid
215:     registration of the feature space.
216:     It should not be confused with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), though CTW uses
217:     DTW.
218: 
219:     It is not required that both time series share the same size, nor the same
220:     dimension (CTW will find a subspace that best aligns feature spaces).
221:     CTW was originally presented in [1]_.
222: 
223:     Parameters
224:     ----------
225:     s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,)
226:         A time series. If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
227:     s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,)
228:         Another time series. If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
229:     max_iter : int (default: 100)
230:         Number of iterations for the CTW algorithm. Each iteration
231:     n_components : int (default: None)
232:         Number of components to be used for Canonical Correlation Analysis.
233:         If None, the lower minimum number of features between seq1 and seq2 is
234:         used.
235:     global_constraint : {"itakura", "sakoe_chiba"} or None (default: None)
236:         Global constraint to restrict admissible paths for DTW calls.
237:     sakoe_chiba_radius : int or None (default: None)
238:         Radius to be used for Sakoe-Chiba band global constraint.
239:         If None and `global_constraint` is set to "sakoe_chiba", a radius of
240:         1 is used.
241:         If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
242:         `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
243:         two. In this case, if `global_constraint` corresponds to no global
244:         constraint, a `RuntimeWarning` is raised and no global constraint is
245:         used.
246:     itakura_max_slope : float or None (default: None)
247:         Maximum slope for the Itakura parallelogram constraint.
248:         If None and `global_constraint` is set to "itakura", a maximum slope
249:         of 2. is used.
250:         If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
251:         `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
252:         two. In this case, if `global_constraint` corresponds to no global
253:         constraint, a `RuntimeWarning` is raised and no global constraint is
254:         used.
255:     verbose : bool (default: True)
256:         If True, scores are printed at each iteration of the algorithm.
257:     be : Backend object or string or None
258:         Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
259:         the NumPy backend is used.
260:         If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
261:         the PyTorch backend is used.
262:         If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
263:         See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
264: 
265:     Returns
266:     -------
267:     float
268:         Similarity score
269: 
270:     Examples
271:     --------
272:     >>> float(ctw([1, 2, 3], [1., 2., 2., 3.]))
273:     0.0
274:     >>> float(ctw([1, 2, 3], [[1., 1.], [2., 2.], [2., 2.], [3., 3.]]))
275:     0.0
276: 
277:     See Also
278:     --------
279:     ctw : Get only the similarity score for CTW
280: 
281:     References
282:     ----------
283:     .. [1] F. Zhou and F. Torre, "Canonical time warping for alignment of
284:        human behavior". NIPS 2009.
285:     """
286:     be = instantiate_backend(be, s1, s2)
287:     s1 = be.array(s1)
288:     s2 = be.array(s2)
289:     return ctw_path(
290:         s1=s1,
291:         s2=s2,
292:         max_iter=max_iter,
293:         n_components=n_components,
294:         global_constraint=global_constraint,
295:         sakoe_chiba_radius=sakoe_chiba_radius,
296:         itakura_max_slope=itakura_max_slope,
297:         verbose=verbose,
298:         be=be,
299:     )[-1]
300: 
301: 
302: def cdist_ctw(
303:     dataset1,
304:     dataset2=None,
305:     max_iter=100,
306:     n_components=None,
307:     global_constraint=None,
308:     sakoe_chiba_radius=None,
309:     itakura_max_slope=None,
310:     n_jobs=None,
311:     verbose=0,
312:     be=None,
313: ):
314:     r"""Compute cross-similarity matrix using Canonical Time Warping (CTW)
315:     similarity measure.
316: 
317:     Canonical Time Warping is a method to align time series under rigid
318:     registration of the feature space.
319:     It should not be confused with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), though CTW uses
320:     DTW.
321: 
322:     It is not required that both time series share the same size, nor the same
323:     dimension (CTW will find a subspace that best aligns feature spaces).
324:     CTW was originally presented in [1]_.
325: 
326:     Parameters
327:     ----------
328:     dataset1 : array-like, shape=(n_ts1, sz1, d) or (n_ts1, sz1) or (sz1,)
329:         A dataset of time series.
330:         If shape is (n_ts1, sz1), the dataset is composed of univariate time series.
331:         If shape is (sz1,), the dataset is composed of a unique univariate time series.
332:     dataset2 : None or array-like, shape=(n_ts2, sz2, d) or (n_ts2, sz2) or (sz2,) (default: None)
333:         Another dataset of time series. 
334:         If `None`, self-similarity of `dataset1` is returned.
335:         If shape is (n_ts2, sz2), the dataset is composed of univariate time series.
336:         If shape is (sz2,), the dataset is composed of a unique univariate time series.
337:     max_iter : int (default: 100)
338:         Number of iterations for the CTW algorithm. Each iteration
339:     n_components : int (default: None)
340:         Number of components to be used for Canonical Correlation Analysis.
